body: The spec's most serious weakness is the synthetic-data fallback. FR-011 permits generating data with 'known ground-truth motion-agency relationships' when no real dataset exists, yet User Stories 2 and 3 place no requirement to distinguish synthetic from real data in modeling, visualization, or interpretation. A regression or random forest fitted to data whose ground truth was authored by the same pipeline cannot yield evidence about human perception of agency; it can only recover the relationship that was installed. At minimum, results derived from synthetic data must be labeled as a methodological demonstration, not findings. A second, related issue: the validation document describes the question as causal ('the causal relationship between visual motion characteristics... and subjective agency'), while the spec itself concedes the design is observational and FR-008 requires associational framing — the artifact's own assumption contradicts the framing under which it was validated. Finally, FR-010's sensitivity analysis is described incoherently: sweeping 'absolute regression coefficient magnitude across a range of small values' ({0.01, 0.05, 0.1}) and reporting how p-values vary tells one nothing about robustness, since p-values are computed from the data, not from an analyst-chosen coefficient cutoff. What varies across those thresholds is only which results one labels 'significant,' which is a decision rule, not an inference.
